subject: Vendor risk transfer & procurement timeline: marketplace vs direct
messages:
From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@finlytics.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@finlytics.com
Date: Sat, 18 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace vs Direct - procurement questions and timeline

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the demo last week — FinLytics is excited by the latency/cost profile you showed. Procurement asked me to follow up with a short list of practical questions so they can decide whether to route this through the AWS Marketplace private offer or sign a direct Redwood Enterprise Agreement. High-level items: 

- Invoice & PO handling: if we go Marketplace (private offer), will Redwood accept our PO and do you support directed invoices to our AP? How long after accepting a private offer does the listing/commit become billable?
- Vendor risk transfer: for direct EA we expect standard indemnity/insurance language to transfer more vendor risk; does that differ materially if we purchase through the marketplace? Any related carve-outs (support, data processing)?
- SOC2 / evidence: procurement requires SOC2 Type II report and an evidence package; does Marketplace procurement delay access to those artifacts versus a direct contract?
- Co-sell and credits: if we route via Marketplace private offer, will Redwood still participate in co-sell and provide co-sell credits to our channel partners?
- Setup lead time & SSO/KMS: how long to enable private offers + VPC/private deployment onboarding vs signing EA and starting a Dedicated trial?

I attached our RFP summary (RFP_FINLYTICS_Q2.pdf) to show the gates. Ideally we need a recommendation by EOD Tue so procurement can present options to their C-suite on Wed. Can you and someone from legal/security join a 30-min sync Monday morning?

Thanks,
Samantha Ortiz
Procurement Lead
FinLytics Inc.
[Attachment: RFP_FINLYTICS_Q2.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@finlytics.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 18 Apr 2026 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace vs Direct - procurement questions and timeline

Samantha — thanks for this and for the RFP. I looked it over and summarized the practical differences below (short bullets for procurement):

1) Invoice & PO handling
- Marketplace private offers: FinLytics creates PO -> Marketplace issues invoice on Redwood's behalf. We support directed invoices / remit-to where supported by the cloud marketplace (typical for AWS private offers). Billable date is usually the private-offer activation date; the marketplace provider needs time to process the purchase (24-72 hours typical).
- Direct EA: Redwood invoices directly per agreed billing schedule. Faster for custom payment terms (net 45/60) but requires Redwood contract signature.

2) Vendor risk transfer / contractual terms
- Marketplace: you generally contract with the marketplace provider (e.g., AWS) and accept a private offer; indemnity and liability are often governed by the private offer terms plus Redwood's terms incorporated by reference — this can limit negotiation breadth. Some customers accept limited warranty/liability caps through marketplace purchases.
- Direct EA: allows full negotiation (indemnity, IP, audit rights, insurance). If FinLytics needs custom indemnities or security carve-outs, direct EA is the safer path.

3) SOC2 & evidence
- We provide the same SOC2 report and evidence pack regardless of purchase route. Access to the artifacts is controlled via our security portal; marketplace purchase does not block access. Note: for supplier attestations that require a contract addendum, direct EA makes the legal attestation process smoother.

4) Co-sell & credits
- Marketplace private offers do not preclude co-sell. We support co-sell with partners for private offers and will still engage for joint GTM and credits, but some marketplace-specific account-level tracking is required to ensure crediting.

5) Setup lead time & technical onboarding
- Private offer activation + payment processing: 1–3 business days typical.
- Private deployment/VPC onboarding (if needed for Dedicated/Private): plan 3–6 weeks depending on KMS/HSM and SSO configuration.
- Direct EA + immediate Dedicated trial: can be faster if you already have a procurement PO and are willing to sign the EA concurrently.

Recommended next step: 30-min call Monday 10am PT to confirm FinLytics' gating items and whether procurement needs negotiation flexibility (if yes -> recommend direct EA). If procurement priorities are speed-to-pay and leveraging channel incentives, private offer via AWS marketplace is viable.

I'll attach a one-pager that frames the decision and a quick mutual action plan template. Lauren, Rishi — please add any legal/security caveats (I'll hand the thread to you).

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-marketplace-vs-direct-one-pager.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@finlytics.com>, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 20 Apr 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace vs Direct - procurement questions and timeline

Hi Samantha — looping in a couple legal/security clarifications so procurement has everything for the Wed review. Quick notes: 

- Marketplace private offers: the commercial terms are transacted via the marketplace private offer; Redwood is still the service provider. For most customers we append a short Order Addendum that references Redwood's Master Terms; however, the marketplace provider's standard terms can limit negotiation of certain indemnity/escrow clauses. If you need broad indemnity (e.g., third-party IP claims), choose direct EA.

- Data processing & audit rights: both routes allow Data Processing Addendums and SOC2 evidence access. If FinLytics requires raw log ingestion for audit or extended retention guarantees, we should capture that in the contract. Direct EA gives more granular control over retention SLAs.

- Co-sell credits: to ensure co-sell crediting when going through marketplace, we need a short GTM registration at deal registration time and to track the purchase order against the co-sell plan. We can support that workflow but timeline for crediting is typically 60–90 days post-close for marketplace transactions (varies by cloud partner).

- Insurance & caps: if FinLytics needs higher caps or specific insurance limits, we will need to negotiate on a direct EA.

Ben — I'll join the Monday call and bring a short legal checklist. Samantha — can you share the specific indemnity/insurance thresholds FinLytics requires so we can pre-check feasibility?

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@finlytics.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, procurement@finlytics.com
Date: Mon, 20 Apr 2026 14:03:00 -07:00

Thanks Ben / Lauren — this is super helpful. Quick answers from our side: 

- Indemnity: FinLytics needs mutual IP indemnity and a $5M cap; if that requires direct EA we can escalate to legal but would like to understand the delta in time.
- Billing terms: FinLytics prefers net-45. If marketplace cannot provide directed invoicing with net-45, we will likely pursue direct EA.
- SOC2: Great that evidence access is the same. We'll still need the SOC2 report for compliance review by Fri.

We can do the Monday slot Ben proposed at 10am PT. For the MA Plan, please include: decision owner (FinLytics procurement), legal approver, estimated activation date for private offer (if chosen), direct EA signature estimate, and any dependencies (SSO, KMS, PO). I attached our PO template for your team to pre-check.

I'll be on the call with our legal counsel (cc'd procurement). See attached PO template.

Best,
Samantha Ortiz

FinLytics Inc.
